title: Fix and flex: the seven aspects
blurb: Say which aspects of performance PRINCE2 Agile fixes and which it flexes, and use that to choose the right response when a project is under pressure.
question: Halfway through a release, a team realizes it cannot finish every planned feature by the fixed date. What does PRINCE2 Agile's approach to fixing and flexing say should happen?

teach.body: Traditional projects often try to fix what is delivered and let time and cost slip. PRINCE2 Agile turns this round. By default, time and cost are fixed with zero tolerance at every level of plan, and what is delivered flexes to fit. Benefits and sustainability are fixed at a minimum and flexed above it. These defaults appear in Table 3.1 of the book.

head: Aspect
Fixed
Flexed
rows: Zero tolerance at all plan levels
Zero tolerance at all plan levels
teach.caption: The five rows quoted in the official V2 rationales. Quality and risk are covered below.

teach.h: Scope: what is fixed and what flexes
teach.caption: MoSCoW prioritization decides where scope can give.

teach.h: Quality, risk and the seven tolerances
teach.body: Under 'manage by exception' every one of the seven aspects (benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability, risk) has tolerances. Quality can also flex: product descriptions, quality specifications and quality tolerances can be prioritized and decomposed so what is delivered flexes while the project stays in control. The working rule is simple: tolerance on what is delivered, none on time and cost.

teach.h: Fix and flex in the progress practice
teach.body: Because time and cost have zero tolerance, there is little point tracking time or cost tolerance in an agile project. Flexibility in what is delivered is the aspect of most interest to the whole project management team, so showing it on a burn chart is natural at any level. If even the Must haves, or minimum benefits or sustainability, are forecast to be missed, that is a forecast tolerance breach: an exception for the level above.

teach.h: The release is running late. What now?

root.label: Forecast: not all features by the fixed date

children.label: Drop or defer Could, then Should items
children.sub: within tolerance; team and PO decide

children.label: Exception to the next level up

teach.body: Greystone Foods is launching a supplier ordering app by a fixed trade-show date. Mid-release, product owner Leah Fairbairn sees the team will not finish everything. She defers two Could-have reports; the date and budget stay put. A cheaper hosting supplier is offered, but it fails the agreed minimum sustainability standard, so project manager Owen Pryce rejects it and trims another Should-have instead. The board hears about it on the project dashboard, not as an exception.

teach.text: Delaying the release to keep every feature breaks the zero tolerance on time. Picking a cheaper supplier that misses the minimum sustainability criteria breaks a fixed minimum. The right lever is almost always scope: drop Could and Should items. Also note the six-aspect 'hexagon' is Version 1: Version 2 has seven aspects.

items: Time and cost: zero tolerance for extra time or cost on all levels of plan.
Scope: fixed for Must haves, flexed for Should and Could haves.
Benefits fixed for minimum viability; sustainability fixed for minimum criteria; both flexed above.
Tolerance on what is delivered; burn charts show it; missing Musts or minimums is an exception.

summary: You can now state the PRINCE2 Agile defaults for time, cost, scope, benefits and sustainability. You can also choose the right response under pressure: flex Should and Could scope, and treat a forecast miss of Musts or minimums as an exception.

A.q: What is the PRINCE2 Agile default tolerance for time?
options: Flexed for Should and Could haves
Zero tolerance on all levels of plan
Fixed at stage level, flexed in teams
Fixed for minimum viability
A.why: Table 3.1: zero tolerance for extra time on all levels of plan.

whyNot.0: Flexing Should and Could haves is the scope default.
whyNot.2: Time is fixed at every level of plan, including team plans.
whyNot.3: Fixed for minimum viability is the benefits default.

A.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile treat scope by default?
options: Fixed for every item in the product backlog
Flexed for every item, including the Musts
Fixed for its minimum criteria, flexed above
Fixed for Musts; flexed for Should and Could
A.why: Table 3.1: scope is fixed for Must haves and flexed for Should and Could haves.

whyNot.0: Fixing everything removes the flexibility agile relies on.
whyNot.1: Must haves are fixed; missing them is an exception.
whyNot.2: Minimum criteria is the sustainability default.

A.q: What is the PRINCE2 Agile default for sustainability?
options: Fixed for minimum criteria, flexed above them
Zero tolerance for it on all levels of plan
Flexed equally for every one of its criteria
Fixed for Must haves, flexed for Could haves
A.why: Table 3.1: sustainability is fixed for minimum criteria and flexed for anything above the minimum criteria.

whyNot.1: Zero tolerance on all levels of plan is the time and cost default.
whyNot.2: The minimum criteria are fixed; only the part above them flexes.
whyNot.3: Must and Could are scope (MoSCoW) terms.

B.q: A board agrees a baseline improvement in delivery accuracy that must be achieved, with room to achieve more. Which aspect and default is this?
options: Scope: fixed for the Must haves
Quality: fixed for acceptance criteria
Benefits: fixed for minimum viability
Sustainability: fixed for minimum criteria
B.why: A baseline improvement with room for more is the benefits target: fixed for minimum viability, flexed above it (1.3.2, Table 3.1).

whyNot.0: Scope concerns which features are delivered, not improvements gained.
whyNot.1: Quality concerns products being fit for purpose.
whyNot.3: Sustainability concerns impact on the wider environment.

B.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile suggest there is little value in tracking time and cost tolerance on a project dashboard?
options: Both are tracked by the delivery teams
Both have zero tolerance by default
Both are reported in the business case
Both flex as scope changes
B.why: With zero tolerance for extra time and cost on all plan levels, tracking their tolerance adds little; what is delivered is the aspect of most interest (12.3.1, Table 3.1).

whyNot.0: The reason is the zero tolerance, not who tracks them.
whyNot.2: Where they are recorded is not the reason.
whyNot.3: Time and cost do not flex; scope does.

B.q: A cheaper supplier would let a team deliver every Should-have item, but it misses the project's minimum sustainability criteria. What fits PRINCE2 Agile's defaults?
options: Use the supplier and keep all Should items
Delay the release to find another supplier
Split the work with the cheaper supplier
Keep the standard and reduce Should items
B.why: Sustainability is fixed at its minimum criteria and time is fixed, so scope (Should and Could) is the aspect to flex (Table 3.1).

whyNot.0: This breaks the fixed minimum sustainability criteria.
whyNot.1: Delaying breaks the zero tolerance on time.
whyNot.2: Using the non-compliant supplier for part of the work still breaks the minimum.

C.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. Benefits are fixed for minimum viability and flexed above it.
2. Cost is flexed for Should and Could haves.
3. Time has zero tolerance for extra time on all levels of plan.
4. Sustainability has zero tolerance on all levels of plan.
options: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4

whyNot.1: Statement 2 is wrong: cost has zero tolerance; Should and Could describes scope.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: cost is fixed and sustainability is fixed only at minimum criteria.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: sustainability is fixed for minimum criteria and flexed above.

C.q: Late in a release, the team forecasts that even the Must-have items cannot be delivered by the fixed date. What should happen, and why?
options: The team extends the iteration, as time can flex here
The PO drops some Musts, as scope tolerance allows it
The PM adds budget, as the cost tolerance covers it
An exception is raised, as tolerance will be exceeded
C.why: Must haves are fixed and time is fixed, so a forecast miss is a tolerance breach: an exception for the next level up (Table 3.1).

whyNot.0: Time has zero tolerance at all plan levels.
whyNot.1: Scope tolerance covers Should and Could haves, not Musts.
whyNot.2: Cost has zero tolerance at all plan levels.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In PRINCE2 Agile, scope is fixed for Must haves and [?] for Should and Could haves.
options: flexed
deferred
baselined
escalated
C.why: Table 3.1: scope is fixed for Musts and flexed for Should and Could haves.

whyNot.1: Items may be deferred as a result, but the Table 3.1 term is flexed.
whyNot.2: Baselining fixes items rather than flexing them.
whyNot.3: Escalation is for forecast tolerance breaches, not for flexing lower priorities.

reteach.title: The fixed train, the flexible luggage
reteach.question: If the train leaves at a fixed time and the fare is fixed, what can change?

blocks.body: A train leaves at 9:00 whatever happens (time fixed) and the ticket is paid (cost fixed). You must take your passport (Must). You would like your camera (Should) and a spare jumper (Could). If you are running late, you leave the jumper, then the camera, but never miss the train or buy a second ticket. You also refuse a shortcut that breaks the rules (sustainability minimum).

blocks.text: The two answers that look helpful but break the defaults: 'give it more time' and 'spend a bit more'.

explain.body: Zero tolerance for extra time and extra cost on all levels of plan (Table 3.1).

test.q: At which levels of plan does PRINCE2 Agile set zero tolerance for extra cost by default?
options: Project level
Stage level
Team level
All levels
test.why: Table 3.1: zero tolerance for extra cost on all levels of plan.

whyNot.0: The project plan is included, but so are stage and team plans.
whyNot.1: Stage plans are included, but so are project and team plans.
whyNot.2: Team plans are included, but so are project and stage plans.

explain.body: Fixed for Must haves; flexed for Should and Could haves (Table 3.1). MoSCoW decides where scope gives.

test.q: Which items may be flexed under PRINCE2 Agile's default for scope?
options: Should and Could haves
Must and Should haves
Must and Could haves
Items marked Won't have
test.why: Scope is flexed for Should and Could haves; Musts are fixed (Table 3.1).

whyNot.2: Could haves flex, but Musts are the fixed part of scope.
whyNot.3: Won't haves are already out of scope for this timeframe.

explain.body: Benefits: fixed for minimum viability, flexed above. Sustainability: fixed for minimum criteria, flexed above (Table 3.1).

test.q: What is the PRINCE2 Agile default for benefits?
options: Zero tolerance on all levels of plan
Fixed for minimum viability, flexed above
Flexed for Should and Could haves
Fixed for minimum criteria, flexed above
test.why: Table 3.1: benefits are fixed for minimum viability and flexed above it.

whyNot.0: Zero tolerance is the time and cost default.
whyNot.2: Should and Could is the scope default.
whyNot.3: Minimum criteria is the sustainability wording.

explain.body: With time and cost fixed, flexibility in what is delivered is the aspect of most interest, so burn charts suit every level (12.3.1).

test.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, which aspect of performance is of most interest to the whole project management team?
options: Cost against the agreed budget
Time against the release plan
Flexibility in what is delivered
Risk against the stage tolerance
test.why: Flexibility in what is delivered is the primary aspect of interest, so displaying it on a burn chart is natural (12.3.1).

whyNot.0: Cost has zero tolerance, so tracking its tolerance adds little.
whyNot.1: Time has zero tolerance, so tracking its tolerance adds little.
whyNot.3: Risk tolerances exist, but the book names what is delivered as the main interest.
